title: Ozi gardens the spoke: automation history through work lugs and paired test lugs
description: Build the spoke-local Ozi gardening model so automation history lives in controller/work/test lugs rather than opaque state receipts. Ozi becomes the spoke gardener: he owns local implementation controllers, orchestrates child work lugs and paired test lugs, and keeps WAI-State.json bounded to runtime/recovery truth.
non_goals: Do not make WAI-State.json the authoritative automation history again
Do not let Octo replace Ozi as the spoke-local executor
Do not invent controller/work/test relationships only in chat; persist them in lugs

must_be_sequential: 1. Define the controller/work/test lug contract for spoke-local automation history.
2. Define the runtime-state boundary so WAI-State.json stays minimal and operational.
3. Apply the model to the initial target area: teaching generation and hub publish flow.
4. Define paired-test expectations and lifecycle gates before ready_for_recheck.
5. Update closeout reconciliation rules so closeout reconciles against Ozi-controlled lugs rather than writing history into state receipts.
can_parallelize: Draft runtime-state boundary in parallel with link-schema contract
Draft paired test policy in parallel with initial teaching/hub example

verification_requirements: Verify controller/work/test relationships are cold-readable from the lug alone
Verify WAI-State.json runtime boundary is explicit and minimal
Verify each work lug requires at least one paired test lug before ready_for_recheck
Verify the teaching-generation and hub-publish example is concrete enough to implement without chat context

acceptance_tests.description: At least one ozi-controller lug exists in WAI-Lugs.jsonl
acceptance_tests.command: python3 -c "import json; lugs=[json.loads(l) for l in open('WAI-Spoke/WAI-Lugs.jsonl') if l.strip()]; ctrl=[l for l in lugs if l.get('type')=='ozi-controller']; print('PASS' if ctrl else 'FAIL — no ozi-controller lugs found')"
acceptance_tests.expected: PASS — at least one ozi-controller lug present

acceptance_tests.description: Every ozi-work lug has a paired ozi-test lug
acceptance_tests.command: python3 -c "import json; lugs=[json.loads(l) for l in open('WAI-Spoke/WAI-Lugs.jsonl') if l.strip()]; work=[l for l in lugs if l.get('type')=='ozi-work']; tests=[l for l in lugs if l.get('type')=='ozi-test']; test_ids={l.get('work_lug_id') for l in tests}; unpaired=[w['id'] for w in work if w.get('id') not in test_ids]; print('PASS' if not unpaired else f'FAIL — unpaired: {unpaired}')"

acceptance_tests.description: WAI-State.json has no automation history keys at top level
acceptance_tests.command: python3 -c "import json; s=json.load(open('WAI-Spoke/WAI-State.json')); bad=[k for k in s if any(x in k.lower() for x in ['history','automation','receipt','ozi_log'])]; print('PASS' if not bad else f'FAIL — history keys: {bad}')"
acceptance_tests.expected: PASS — WAI-State.json stays clean of automation history

review_questions: Is Ozi clearly scoped to spoke-local gardening while Octo remains wheel-level?
Are controller/work/test link rules specific enough for a future implementer?
Is the runtime-vs-history boundary durable enough to keep state lean?

review_history.summary: Lug is conceptually sound and boundary is clear (Ozi spoke-local, Octo wheel-level). Three gaps filled in this cycle: (1) controller/work/test lug schema added to lug_schema field — builder now has exact field names and id formats; (2) concrete teaching-generation example added to concrete_example field showing a full controller/work_1/work_2/test_lug chain; (3) all three acceptance_tests replaced with runnable Python/shell commands. runtime-vs-history boundary is clear: WAI-State.json non-goal is explicit and acceptance test 3 verifies it. Ready for builder to claim.
recommendations: Builder must create ozi-controller, ozi-work, and ozi-test lugs for each Ozi automation batch — do not use session-summary or autosave types for Ozi history.

The sequence step 5 (update closeout reconciliation) means: closeout Step 1 should look for ozi-controller lugs when reconciling, not just autosave lugs. Additive change — do not remove existing autosave reconciliation.
WAI-State.json changes (templates/spoke/WAI-State.json) are minimal: add ozi section to _session_state for current controller id and last ozi run timestamp only.

workflow.handoff_reason: Implementer review + gap fill complete. Builder can claim after octo-gardener-dispatch ships.

progress: ✅ Elevated compact spoke-gardening design into a canonical implementation lug
✅ Linked it conceptually to Octo's wheel-gardening dispatch architecture
✅ Preserved the old compact lug as design/source material

lug_schema._note: Canonical schema for Ozi spoke-gardening lugs. All three types live in WAI-Lugs.jsonl.

controller_lug._note: One Ozi automation pass or bounded task batch

required_fields.title: What Ozi is orchestrating
required_fields.target_lug_id: implementation or task lug being worked

work_lug._note: One discrete unit of work dispatched by an Ozi controller

required_fields.task: concise description of what was done

test_lug._note: Paired verification record. Required before any ozi-work lug can move to ready_for_recheck.

required_fields.test_command: runnable shell or python verification command

concrete_example._note: Teaching-generation and hub-publish flow using the controller/work/test pattern
